title: Recording: The Lord Loves The One (That Loves The Lord) by George Harrison | 1972
content:
Apple Studios, London
Producer: George Harrison
Engineer: Phil McDonald

The main recording sessions for George Harrison’s fourth solo album, Living In The Material World, began on 2 October 1972.

The first song worked on was ‘The Lord Loves The One (That Loves The Lord)’. It was inspired by AC Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, the founder and leader of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON), the Hare Krishna movement.

‘The Lord Loves The One (That Loves The Lord)’ I wrote after Swami AC Bhaktivedanta came to my house one afternoon. His life is an example to us all. The things that most people are struggling for is fame or fortune or wealth or position: always that’s their main ambition and desire in life, to be rich or famous or to have a good reputation, and really none of that is important because in the end, death will take it all away. So you spend your life struggling for something which is in effect a waste of time. After talking with Swamiji about all that I wrote the song ‘Lord Loves The One’.
George Harrison
I Me Mine

Although not credited as a producer, Phil Spector was present during the session, suggesting that his involvement was not formally defined at this stage.

The basic track had Klaus Voormann’s bass guitar on track one, Jim Keltner’s drums on two and three, and Harrison’s acoustic guitar on five, and his vocals on 10. Early takes had Gary Wright’s electric piano on track six, but subsequent attempts had it moved to seven and eight.

Early takes were at a faster tempo than the final version, and Harrison expressed some uncertainty as to the song’s ending. He discussed fading it out with a saxophone or bass guitar solo, and Spector suggested giving it a definitive finish.

Most of the early takes were incomplete, but by take 20 the tempo had slowed and Harrison was feeling satisfied with the arrangement. Take 23 was the final attempt and became the album master.
